title: Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, impact dozens of organizations
content_md: ConnectWise is investigating an active malware campaign targeting managed service providers (MSPs) that uses compromised ScreenConnect environments to deploy rogue remote-access clients to customer devices. The campaign was first discovered Wednesday by cybersecurity firm Huntress, which says it has identified six compromised MSPs and 286 affected endpoints across 47 organizations, and that the number of victims continues to rise. "Our SOC is working an active campaign that started around 17:47 UTC today targeting cloud-hosted ScreenConnect instances," Huntress posted to Reddit. "We are currently tracking 6 compromised MSPs and 286+ endpoints, and those numbers are climbing. ConnectWise is engaged and working this with us." ScreenConnect is a remote access and support platform used by MSPs and IT teams to remotely manage and troubleshoot customer devices. According to Huntress, attackers are using ScreenConnect's Run Command functionality to deploy ScreenConnect clients on managed endpoints, providing remote access outside of the legitimate MSP's ScreenConnect environment. The researchers also warned of a potentially more dangerous technique in which attackers can compromise an MSP technician's workstation when they initiate a ScreenConnect session with an infected customer device. It is unclear how this reported reverse-pivot technique works, including whether it exploits a software vulnerability or abuses legitimate ScreenConnect functionality. In a statement to BleepingCom
